# How this wiki works

This wiki is a small static site that lives in the repo under `wiki/` and is published by GitHub Pages. There is no build step and no framework: it is plain HTML, CSS and ES module JavaScript, with three libraries (marked, DOMPurify, highlight.js) loaded from a CDN with a vendored fallback.

Every page is a **board**: a free canvas of cards you position yourself. You edit the board on the live site and **Save** commits the JSON straight back to the repo through the GitHub API, so the published site updates on the next Pages build.

## Files

- `index.html`, the shell: sidebar, toolbar, board and inspector.
- `css/style.css`, the whole theme, one set of tokens on `:root`.
- `js/app.js`, wires everything together (state, sidebar, save flow, paste, menus).
- `js/board.js`, the canvas: renders cards, drag, resize, z order, freehand draw.
- `js/cards.js`, the card model and per type renderers (text/code/image/video/table/shape/draw).
- `js/inspector.js`, the per card editor on the right.
- `js/github.js`, the only code that writes to the network, via the GitHub Contents API.
- `js/icons.js`, inline Lucide icons.
- `pages/index.json`, the page list with categories. `pages/<slug>.json`, one board each.
- `assets/`, uploaded images and video, committed through the API.

## Saving back to the repo

**Save** asks once for a fine grained GitHub token with Contents read and write on this repo. The token is stored only in your browser `localStorage` and is only ever sent to `api.github.com`. ## Interactions

- **Right click the board** or press **Shift+A** to add a card where you point.
- **Drag** a card by its header, **resize** from any edge or corner.
- **Right click a card** to collapse it, hide it from the published page, restack it, or delete it. Select and press **Delete** to remove it.
- **Paste** an image, gif or SVG straight onto the board in edit mode.
- **Right click a page** in the sidebar to rename it, set its category, or delete it.
- Text cards render **Markdown, BBCode or HTML**, all sanitized before display.
